doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Policing, protests and the Minneapolis killing
summary: Baron discusses militarized police, peaceful protest, rioting as the language of the unheard, and what to do now.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: It’s here. Everything is like, no more. And here the answer is, I’m not saying all police are bad, but the answer for a lot of the municipalities is like you know their police get wartime army weapons. You know that’s somehow — the illegality of that has been circumvented. Or maybe it’s not illegal everywhere. And it’s just gotten so like Trump’s feeling about it is I’m going to have law and order I don’t care how many people I have to kill or tear gas. It’s just absurd, his rule, it’s totally absurd. He’s a monarch in his eyes and he feels like he could do anything he wants. But then there are good people, I love the fact that some of the reports about the good police that are standing with the demonstrators. Demonstrations shouldn’t be seen as an affront to our peacetime. Demonstrations are the right of the people. Peaceful assembly. Now I’ve even heard reports some of the people that are showing up and looting and rioting have been sought out to do that. There is a group of people that does it automatically but it’s not the people that are trying to speak a message. I’m not going to get the quote perfect but Martin Luther King said rioting is the language of the unheard. Maybe that is it, what he said. I mean people are not — when — God I can’t think of his name, for selling cigarettes in Staten Island and the police killed him with a choke hold. That was like six years ago.
And it just like we have a chance, and I know people with skin this color are like trying to figure out what do we do now.
